qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Lacks a structural moat archetype ('None'). Consumer tissue and basic hygiene products face intense private-label competition from European grocers. Multi-year GAAP ROIC sits chronically below the 12% hurdle (~6.5-8.5%), and price increases persistently lag volatile pulp and energy feedstock cost spikes, causing periodic operating margin compression.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (3a = None, 3b = N, REJECT). European hygiene and tissue manufacturer lacking structural moat defenses against supermarket private-label penetration. 10-year average GAAP ROIC hovers around 6.5-8.5% (failing the 12% hurdle), and margins experience extreme volatility during pulp and energy cost inflation cycles.
qualitative.evidence: Spun off from SCA in 2017. Segments include Health & Medical (TENA, Leukoplast), Consumer Goods (Lotus, Tempo, Zewa, Cushelle), and Professional Hygiene (Tork). Operating margin compressed to 5.5% in 2022 during pulp/energy spike before recovering to 12.4% in 2025. Long-term GAAP ROIC averages 6.5-8.0%, failing the Munger moat capital efficiency test.
